# Vapour fraction from the Rachford-Rice equation

`eos.rachford_rice`

## Source

**Nielsen, L. (2023)**

`RachfordRice.calcBetaNielsen2023` from NeqSim 3.20.0, minus the single-phase dispatch: NeqSim answers a root outside `[0, 1]` with the `phaseFractionMinimumLimit` clamp, and this returns the root.

DOI: [10.2118/952327-G](https://doi.org/10.2118/952327-G)


## Algorithm

A model rather than a calculation: what this page pins down is the procedure,
not an equation, and both implementations read it from here.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Scheme | `rachford_rice_nielsen_2023` |
| Convergence | `absolute` |
| Tolerance | `1e-10` |
| Max iterations | `300` |
| Initialisation | `vapour_fraction_one_half` |

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `z` | dimensionless | the overall mole fractions of the feed |
| `K` | dimensionless | the K-values `K_i = y_i / x_i` at the state the split is asked about, positive. A value below `1e-30` marks an ion, which is skipped. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `beta` | dimensionless | the vapour fraction. Inside `[0, 1]` it is the split; outside it is the negative flash, and the caller decides what that means. A feed whose K-values do not straddle one returns `1e-12` at the end it lies towards. |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `K > 0` | raises | the solver takes the reciprocal of `K` and of `1 - K`, so zero and below have no meaning |

## Assumptions

- `g(beta) = sum_i z_i (K_i - 1) / (1 + beta (K_i - 1)) = 0`, the material balance of a two-phase split written in the vapour fraction. Its root in the physical bracket is unique and strictly decreasing there, so a bracketed Newton converges from any point inside.
- the bracket is the poles of `g`: `max over K_i > 1 of 1/(1 - K_i) < beta < min over K_i < 1 of 1/(1 - K_i)`. It exists only when the K-values straddle one, so a missing bracket proves the feed single phase rather than a failure to find one.
- NeqSim's `RachfordRice` carries two solvers behind a static `method` field. This ports `calcBetaNielsen2023`, the default: nothing in NeqSim 3.20.0 calls `setMethod`, so every flash in the library runs it. `calcBetaMichelsen2001` is reachable only directly, and is named here rather than ported.
- Nielsen & Lia solve the equation in a rescaled pair, `a = (alpha - alpha_min)/(alpha_max - alpha)`, `b = 1/(alpha - alpha_min)` for `alpha = 1/(1 - K)`, and in `1/K` when the root is above one half. The reformulation avoids round-off; it is not a different equation.
- a component with `K_i < 1e-30` is an ion and is skipped: it stays in the liquid and does not take part in the split. NeqSim's threshold and NeqSim's reason.
- NeqSim's `calcBeta` clamps its answer to `[1e-12, 1 - 1e-12]` and declines to iterate when the root would fall outside `[0, 1]`. Neither is ported: the root comes back as the equation gives it, so the negative flash stays visible, and `1e-12` is the answer only where no root exists.
- a K-value of exactly one contributes nothing: `z_i (K_i - 1)` is zero in every term, and the solver drops it through the same denominator floor NeqSim uses. A feed of nothing but such components is the trivial solution `x = y = z`, and this answers it with the lower clamp.
- `z` and `K` are checked for length and for a positive `K` rather than adjusted: a K-value of zero or below makes the reciprocal in the solver meaningless.
- azoth's flashes do not call this. NeqSim stops at `1e-10` on its two rescaled residuals, about `1e-11` in `beta`; `eos.pt_flash` asserts the residual of every answer at `1e-12` and so keeps its own bisection. Two procedures for one equation, standing side by side.

## References

- Rachford, H. H.; Rice, J. D. (1952). "Procedure for Use of Electronic Digital Computers in Calculating Flash Vaporization Hydrocarbon Equilibrium." Journal of Petroleum Technology 4(10), 19-3. DOI 10.2118/952327-G
- Nielsen, L. (2023). "Avoiding round-off error in the Rachford-Rice equation." The reformulation `calcBetaNielsen2023` ports.
- NeqSim - https://github.com/equinor/neqsim - Apache-2.0. `thermodynamicoperations/flashops/RachfordRice`, `calcBetaNielsen2023`, its ion skip, its `1e-10` tolerance and its `300`-iteration cap ported verbatim; its two single-phase returns are not.
